thread:
leo: Heads up — staging docs build failed on deploy: a bunch of broken fragment links in /guides/runtime.md after the navbar path tidy.
leo: Error in CI log: `404 anchor not found: #runtime~cache-behavior` (we don't have any anchors with `~` in our headings AFAICT).
marnie: can you paste the exact markdown snippet where the link originates?
leo: sure — it's in the 'Caching and KV' subsection, link uses relative reference: `[cache behavior](#runtime~cache-behavior)`
leo: i think that `~` came from an automated relpath rewrite script that replaces spaces with `~` for some legacy links.
docs-ci: build log excerpt:
```
WARN: LinkCheck failed: file=guides/runtime.md, target=#runtime~cache-behavior
Info: slugify('Runtime / Cache Behavior') -> 'runtime-cache-behavior'
```
sam: that slugify -> `runtime-cache-behavior` vs link with `~` explains it. looks like the relpath normalizer is using a different slug scheme.
frank: i've seen this when earlier migration scripts encoded tildes for nested headings. quick fix options: 1) change the link to the canonical slug, 2) add explicit heading id in the md (`### Cache Behavior {#runtime~cache-behavior}`) or 3) adjust the normalizer.
marnie: prefer option 1 for quick patch. we should avoid adding weird explicit ids unless necessary.
leo: opened PR with fix (link change) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 (small patch to 1 line). pinging for review.
frank: quick review done, looks good. main question: do we need a follow-up to audit the normalizer?
sam: yes — I'm opening a tracking issue to prevent regressions. tagging eng-runtime and docs infra.
sam: ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/456 — notes: normalizer should use mkdocs/docusaurus slug rules (dash-separated, lowercase, strip punctuation).
docs-ci: re-run triggered by PR merge.
ops-bot: deploy-staging started for branch `pr-789` by leo.
docs-ci: staging build passed — all fragment links resolved.
leo: thanks all — will schedule the normalizer audit next week, adding sam + frank. :thumbsup:
